ARISTO

# PHARMACEUTICALS PRIVATE LIMITED

Ref 1008/CIR/322

Date: 18.09.2025

To:

All Stockists, Distributors, and Trade Partners

Subject: Mandatory Reduction in Prices (MRP) and Compliance with GST Rate Revision - Passing

Benefits to Patients under Para 25 of DPCO 2013.

Dear Trade Partners,

As communicated as per the notification by the GST Council, the rate of Goods and Services Tax (GST) applicable to pharmaceutical products are being reduced from 12% to 5% with effect from 22° September, 2025 for majority of Drugs/Formulations (except formulations as mentioned in annexure II) and Food Products GST are reduced from 18% / 12% to 5%.

In view of this development, we wish to apprise you of the following key points, which require your immediate attention and compliance:

1. Revision of Product MRPs and Form V Filing

- The downward revision in GST rates mandates a corresponding reduction in the Maximum Retail Prices (MRP) of all affected products.
- As per legal requirements, revised prices in Form V under Drugs (Price Control) Order2013 are being filed and will be applicable effective 22.09.2025. You may kindly note that, after transition to new GST rates, our price to stockist (exclusive of GST) and price to retailer (exclusive of GST) will remain unchanged. Also the trade margins of all our products will remain unchanged.

2. Statutory Requirement to Pass on Benefits

- Passing on the benefft of reduced taxes to the end consumer is mandatory under Para 25 of the Drugs (Prices Control) Order, 2013.
- ITC eligibility for existing stock remains unaffected; however, any benefit accrued due to GST reduction must be transferred to patients through adjusted pricing.
- While some stocks would bear old MRP's even on 22.09.2025, we request you to inform all your chemists to sell strictly the medicines at revised lower MRP from 22.09.2025.
- The benefit of lower MRP should be passed down to the final consumer through the stockist and retailer supply chain.
- It is highly recommended and expected that, our Price List (Annexure I/11/III) is displayed in a conspicuous (visible) part of your premises.

3. Input Tax Credit (ITC) and Inventory Handling

- Working formulas for the stocks in hand at Retail level is given in "Note" section of this circular.
- Full Input Tax Credit will be available on the closing stock purchased at the earlier GST rate. There is no financial loss or risk of ITC lapsing; adjustments can be made in subsequent GST returns.
- All invoices from 22nd September 2025 onwards must reflect the new GST rate and revised MRP.
